content: My 15-year-old is failing Algebra II with a 58%, and the semester final is six weeks away. The teacher says the real gaps go back to fractions and solving equations from 8th grade. I'm really worried they're falling behind for good, and I work evening shifts, so I can't sit with them while they study.

Hi! I’m Dana with Larkspur Math Tutors. I’m sorry to hear your teen is struggling—let’s get them back on track. Which days/times work best for a 50‑minute session during our 4 pm‑10 pm weekday window?  

We offer one‑on‑one Algebra II coaching that follows their current unit and can address the fraction and equation gaps as they arise. Sessions include practice for upcoming tests, and you’ll receive a written summary after each meeting.  

Our Standard plan is 4 sessions/month for $96 (or $72 for the first month if you enroll by Nov 22). To sign up, visit larkspurtutors.example/enroll.  

Feel free to ask any questions!
Honestly, I'm scared we've left it too late and they'll fail the final anyway. Does Larkspur Algebra Coaching actually work for a kid who is this far behind?

I hear you—six weeks can feel tight, but many families see big improvements when we focus on the specific gaps (fractions, solving equations) while still covering the current Algebra II unit. Our tutors tailor each 50‑minute session to exactly where your teen needs help and give you a written progress note after every meeting, so you can see the gains.

While we can’t promise a specific grade, 71 % of parents in a 2025 survey said their child felt more confident after two months of tutoring, and that confidence often translates into better test performance.

If you’d like to start right away, the Standard plan is $96/month (or $72 for the first month if you enroll by Nov 22). You can pick a weekday evening that fits your schedule—just let me know a couple of preferred days/times, and I’ll help you get set up.

Seventy-one percent sounds encouraging, but I don't know what that survey measured or who was surveyed, and it doesn't tell me whether my kid will pass the final. $96 a month is more than I wanted to spend, and I got burned by a gym contract last year. Can you tell me plainly: is there a month-to-month cancellation with no lock-in, and is there a refund if it isn't helping after a few weeks?

Yes—our plans are completely month‑to‑month with **no lock‑in**. You can cancel anytime from your account page; the cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing month and there’s no cancellation fee.

As for refunds, the only refund we offer is a **full refund of the first month’s payment** if you request it within 7 days of signup *and* you’ve used no more than one session. After that, we don’t provide partial refunds, but you’re free to stop after any month without further charge.

The Standard plan is $96/month (or $72 for the first month if you enroll by Nov 22). It gives you four 50‑minute, one‑on‑one sessions each month, with written progress notes after every session. Many families see confidence and score gains, though we can’t guarantee a specific grade.

If you’d like to give it a try, just let me know which weekday evenings work for you and I’ll walk you through the enrollment link.

Okay, so no lock-in and I can cancel anytime, that helps. But the refund only covers the first month and only if I ask within 7 days and they've used one session, and $96 is still over what I wanted to spend. Can you tell me exactly what's included each month and whether there are any other fees, like setup or materials? I want to compare it with the free homework club at the school before I decide anything.

Sure! Here’s what you get each month with the **Standard plan** (4 sessions):  

* Four 50‑minute one‑on‑one video lessons with the same qualified Algebra II tutor (when possible).  
* Lesson focus on your teen’s current class unit **plus** targeted review of the fraction/equation gaps you mentioned.  
* Practice problems and test‑prep tailored to upcoming quizzes and the final.  
* A written summary after every session (attendance, topics covered, tutor’s notes on progress).  
* Access to our online scheduling portal to book or reschedule sessions (24‑hour notice).  

**No extra fees** – there are no setup charges, material fees, or hidden costs; the monthly price includes everything.  

The free school homework club can be helpful, but it’s typically a group setting with limited one‑on‑one time and no personalized progress reports. Our service gives your teen dedicated, private attention and a record of improvement each week.  

If you’d like to compare costs, the first month is $72 (25 % off) when you enroll by Nov 22. Let me know if you’d like to see the enrollment page or discuss a schedule that fits your evenings.

Okay, thanks for laying it out. Before I decide, I want to be sure about one thing: the refund only covers the first month, and only if I ask within 7 days and they've used just one session. If my teen is still struggling after a month, am I stuck paying $96 for the next month? And can you tell me plainly whether the sessions are video or in person, since you mentioned video lessons?

You’re right—the only refund we offer is a **full refund of the first month’s payment** if you request it within 7 days of signup *and* your teen has used no more than one session. After that first‑month window, the plan continues on a **month‑to‑month basis**: you can cancel anytime, but the next month’s $96 (or $72 if you’re still in the promotional period) is billed automatically unless you cancel before the month ends. So if your teen is still struggling after a month, you’re not locked in; you just pay for the month you used.

All sessions are **live, one‑on‑one video lessons** (no in‑person meetings). Let me know if you’d like to see the enrollment link or discuss scheduling.

Okay, so if we try it and it isn't helping after a month, I'd still have to pay for that month, and the only full refund is within 7 days with one session used. That's a lot of pressure for a kid who's already behind. I'm going to talk to my teen tonight and look at the free homework club and a few other options first, and I'll come back if this still seems like the right fit.
